newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends higher on weak output forecasts.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends higher on weak output forecasts.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled sharply higher on Friday on stop-loss buying after weaker-than-expected forecasts of Japan's industrial output for June and July.

The rally was also fuelled by comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita earlier in the afternoon which were seen as less positive on the economic recovery than the market interpretation of Wednesday's BOJ "tankan" survey.

"It was the first chance for us to hear the BOJ governor speak after Wednesday's stronger-than-expected tankan. But he didn't make any bullish comments on the economy. Instead, it seems he tried to tone down the way we interpreted the tankan," said an interest rate swap (IRS) dealer at a city bank.
Matsushita said if the official discount rate was raised prematurely it would negatively affect the economy, which could in turn push down long-term yields.
His statement was in reference to a general argument that Japan's low interest rates are exposing people dependent on interest rate income to a severe financial situation.

"Short positions were built up after Wednesday's tankan and again this afternoon after the surprising rise in May output. But these shorts were mostly squeezed after the following forecasts for June and July," said a long-term bank dealer.
The Trade Ministry said industrial output in May rose a preliminary 3.8 percent from the previous month, prompting initial selling. The March briefly fell as low as 98.72.

But the ministry also said it forecast a 2.6 percent month-on-month fall for June and a 0.9 percent rise for July, both weaker than the market had expected. The March settled at 98.86, just off Friday's session high of 98.87.
Turnover of March futures was a large 122,562 contracts.
A further rally is unlikely for the March after it regained around half of the ground it lost during a sharp fall on Wednesday from 98.98 to 98.72, the long-term bank dealer said.
"The contract is likely to consolidate for the time being because there is no fresh factor in sight next week," he said.

Traders said a BOJ rate rise is unlikely even if the U.S. raises interest rates around the time Federal Open Market Committe meets next week. They said the BOJ governor's comments implied that the bank will rather focus on domestic private-sector activity than on exchange rates.

IRS rates fell across the board in the afternoon in line with fading fears of an imminent rate hike. The three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.53/1.57 percent in late Tokyo, down sharply from Thursday's 1.63/1.67 percent.

The key overnight call rate eased to 0.49 percent from Thursday's 0.52 due to the BOJ's more accommodative operation. It was the first time since June 11 that the BOJ conducted an operation leaving a market surplus of some 300 billion yen.
Meanwhile, one- and two-week interbank rates rose to 0.60 and 0.61 respectively due to banks' strong fund demand covering the month end, traders said. -- Risa Maeda +81-33432-8570
